comparator.name: Global Communication Science
comparator.sourceNotes: UvA distinguishes the English Global Communication Science track from Dutch Communicatiewetenschap. The English study-programme table supplies 60 EC in each year. Year 1 contains seven compulsory courses (12+12+6+6+8+8+8 EC). Year 2 contains five 6-EC theory/research/practice courses, a 24-EC internationally oriented internship and a 6-EC internship case. Year 3 combines 30 EC of genuine open elective/minor/exchange space, one 6-EC communication-topic restricted elective, an 18-EC independent research project and 6 EC From Research to Impact. The named topic examples are not assigned as compulsory content; the 6-EC restricted choice is retained generically.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names the English Global Communication Science track; UvA explicitly contrasts its international and cross-cultural focus with the Dutch Communicatiewetenschap track. This exact route is chosen independently of UCR fit.

alternatives.label: Global media, communication and research
alternatives.concept: Study how media and public messages shape debates across societies. Combine media history and analysis, persuasion and climate communication with surveys, experiments and qualitative research.
alternatives.labelReason: Media forms, public messages and cross-border issues organise the media, communication and research-methods sequence.
progression: Media, communication and method introductions precede advanced persuasion, documentary and organisational study where feasible; six semesters, formal prerequisites, availability and six 300-level courses were verified against the current enriched workbook.

alternatives.label: International communication and audience strategy
alternatives.concept: Study how organisations understand audiences and make communication decisions. Combine media and persuasion with market research, consumer engagement, international business and organisational psychology.
alternatives.labelReason: Market research, consumer design, business foundations, international business and leadership under pressure give a distinct organisational emphasis.
alternatives.distinctness: Five courses and 37.5 EC differ in each direction. The organisation-focused option adds market research, consumer design, business foundations, international business and leadership under pressure. The broad option adds international relations, sociology, media history, environmental media and youth resilience.
progression: Research and venture foundations precede Market Research in the fourth term. Rhetoric in Action follows introductory rhetoric in the sixth term. The two courses are offered in their revised terms.

candidates.label: Health and sustainability communication
candidates.rationale: Climate Crisis and Media & the Environment contribute environmental messaging. Available health and sustainability courses add issue context but do not build a sustained sequence in health communication or cross-cultural evaluation of campaigns.

selection.assessment: The two accepted programmes differ in their public-media and organisational-audience purposes. A third health and sustainability communication programme would require more sustained communication study than the available direct subject courses support.

blocks: Both examine changes in media and their social consequences. UCR follows American media and storytelling; UvA compares global digital production, algorithms, privacy and regulation.
No selected UCR course directly covers the specific UvA Communication Theme 2: Crises & Resilience requirement at its stated scope and credit weight; this distinct component remains visible.
UCR media and social psychology courses contribute to parts of the subject. No single selected course covers comparative communication-science theories across societies.
Both introduce research designs, data collection and statistical inference. UCR applies these skills in a general research project; UvA uses communication-science examples and SPSS.
Both develop experimental reasoning and analysis of human behaviour. UCR emphasises experimental design and statistical models; UvA also has students conduct a communication survey.
Both teach qualitative research design, interviews, focus groups and interpretation. UCR also covers ethnography and visual methods, while UvA focuses on intercultural communication research.

Both study public communication about sustainability. UCR focuses on climate messages and participation in public debate; UvA also examines health across cultures.
Both study persuasive marketing and audience engagement. UCR develops consumer and brand strategy; UvA also studies entertainment, influencers and differences across markets.

notes.text: UvA requires a sequence in communication research, a 24-EC internship and an 18-EC independent research project. UCR builds related skills through media, rhetoric and empirical research courses. Its optional independent research sits outside the scheduled 180 EC.

audience.programmeDescription: Global Communication Science at the University of Amsterdam studies how media and communication shape people and societies across cultures. Students practise research methods and apply them through a supervised internship and an independent project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The first UCR option combines media, public communication and research methods. The second uses related tools to study how organisations understand and engage audiences.
